title: PortOS: Border Traffic Orchestration AIP Agent
description: AIP Agent on Palantir Foundry that shifts CBP Port of Entry operations from reactive to predictive — projected 52% wait-time reduction.
fullDescription: PortOS is an end-to-end AIP Agent built on Palantir Foundry that helps U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) shift land Port of Entry operations from reactive to predictive. The agent ingests 7 datasets covering crossing events, officer shifts, non-intrusive inspection (NII) system status, and port configurations, organizing them into a 5-object ontology (Port, CrossingEvent, OfficerShift, Alert, NiiSystem) with 4 link types for relational reasoning. Three decision functions drive the system: a TypeScript surge detector that flags abnormal crossing volume, a TypeScript lane-configuration recommender that suggests optimal lane mixes, and an AIP Logic wait-time predictor. Two automations trigger real-time alerts surfaced in an operations dashboard when predicted wait times breach thresholds. The narrative demonstrates a shift from a 95-minute reactive response to a 45-minute predictive intervention — a projected 52% reduction — grounded in real CBP BWT, DHS OIG, BTS, and GSA data sources.
challenges: Working within Foundry's DevTier constraints (v2 TypeScript Functions only accept string parameters, not ObjectSet), and grounding every operational claim in real federal data sources — CBP Border Wait Times, DHS OIG-25-27, BTS, and GSA — rather than fabricated numbers.
learnings: Learned Palantir Foundry's ontology-driven development model end-to-end: Pipeline Builder for data ingestion, Ontology Manager for object/link modeling, AIP Logic for declarative decision functions, Actions for write-backs, and Agent Studio for orchestrating LLM-driven operational workflows. Developed intuition for when to use code-based TypeScript functions vs. declarative AIP Logic, and how to connect real-time data to agent decision-making.

title: Multi-Agent AI Assistant System
description: Multi-agent AI system with 2 specialized agents delivering sub-5-second response times, featuring interactive CLI and conversation memory.
fullDescription: Built a multi-agent AI system with Microsoft's AutoGen 0.6.1 and OpenAI's GPT-4o featuring a five-layer architecture (UI, Memory, Orchestration, Agents, External Services) with 2 specialized agents delivering sub-5-second response times. Created a custom CLI using the Rich library, implemented SQLite-backed conversation memory with session tracking, and set up proper configuration and logging. The system integrates with Open-Meteo and Tavily APIs. Designed the SQLite schema with indexes for conversation analytics and used context managers for transaction handling and data consistency.
challenges: Implementing robust asynchronous programming with AutoGen's multi-agent orchestration, designing database connection management with context managers to prevent SQLite file locking, and creating multi-layer error handling for graceful degradation during API failures.
learnings: Gained deep expertise in multi-agent AI systems, async Python programming patterns, production-grade configuration and logging practices, database transaction management, and building user-friendly CLI interfaces. Learned to balance cutting-edge AI technology (AutoGen, GPT-4o) with software engineering best practices for maintainable, scalable systems.

title: Gaussian Time Series MLOps Pipeline
description: MLOps pipeline achieving R² = 1.0 and MAE of 10.4 on 132 months of call center data with automated CI/CD on AWS.
fullDescription: Built a production-grade MLOps pipeline using Gaussian Process Regression that achieved R² = 1.0 and MAE of 10.4 across 132 months of historical call center data. The system features a staged deployment workflow (staging -> manual approval -> production) using Terraform for infrastructure-as-code, Docker for containerization, and AWS CodePipeline for fully automated CI/CD. The Flask REST API serves predictions with confidence intervals, deployed on AWS Lightsail containers.
challenges: Implementing a robust staging-to-production workflow with manual approval gates, provisioning complete ML infrastructure via Terraform, and ensuring consistent deployments across environments.
learnings: Gained expertise in MLOps best practices, Terraform for ML infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines for machine learning, and containerization of ML models for production deployment.

title: Clinical Analytics with Snowflake ML
description: Healthcare analytics pipeline with ML monitoring, data drift detection, and automated model retraining using Snowflake.
fullDescription: Implemented a production-grade ML monitoring and retraining pipeline for healthcare analytics using Snowflake as the data warehouse. The system detects data drift using multiple statistical tests (Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Chi-Square, Population Stability Index, Jensen-Shannon Divergence, Wasserstein Distance) and monitors model performance metrics (Precision, Recall, ROC-AUC) to trigger automated retraining when degradation is detected.
challenges: Implementing comprehensive drift detection using multiple statistical methods, designing conditional retraining triggers, and integrating with Snowflake for enterprise data warehousing.
learnings: Developed expertise in ML monitoring beyond simple accuracy tracking, statistical testing for distribution shifts, Snowflake integration, and building automated retraining pipelines.

title: Real-Time E-Commerce Observability Stack
description: Real-time data pipeline and observability platform for e-commerce with Kafka, Spark, InfluxDB, and Grafana dashboards.
fullDescription: Built a complete real-time observability stack for e-commerce platforms. The system processes live customer activity events through Kafka with Avro serialization, enriches streams with MySQL demographic data via Spark Structured Streaming, stores metrics in InfluxDB time-series database, and visualizes real-time analytics through Grafana dashboards. Includes both Java and Python implementations with full Docker Compose deployment.
challenges: Implementing stream-batch joins for real-time enrichment, managing Avro schema evolution with Confluent Schema Registry, and building a complete observability stack with multiple integrated services.
learnings: Gained expertise in streaming architecture patterns, Avro serialization with schema registry, Grafana dashboard development, and building production-grade observability platforms.

title: Cloud-Native Multimodal RAG System
description: Building a multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation system combining textual and visual data for context-aware food recommendations.
fullDescription: Currently building a multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system that combines textual and visual data to generate context-aware food recommendations. This project leverages AWS Bedrock, S3, and FAISS for cloud-native data storage, vectorization, and scalable similarity search. The system features a Streamlit-based chatbot that enables cross-modal search through Claude-Sonnet Multimodal LLM, allowing users to query with both text and images.
challenges: Integrating multimodal data sources and ensuring accurate cross-modal retrieval while maintaining low latency for real-time recommendations.
learnings: Gained hands-on experience with AWS cloud services, vector databases, and the practical implementation of RAG architectures for production use cases.

title: Real-Time Big Data Pipeline on AWS
description: Real-time data pipeline on AWS processing COVID-19 API data every 5 minutes with interactive dashboards.
fullDescription: Designed and deployed a real-time data pipeline on AWS to process COVID-19 API data every 5 minutes, leveraging Apache NiFi for ingestion and encryption, and Kafka for distributed message streaming. Implemented PySpark jobs to transform and clean streaming data, writing outputs to HDFS and exposing curated data through Hive external tables for analytics. Automated pipeline scheduling using Apache Airflow, ensuring fault-tolerant execution across AWS EC2 nodes. Delivered interactive KPI dashboards in Tableau and AWS QuickSight, visualizing confirmed, recovered, and fatal case trends by region.
challenges: Ensuring fault-tolerant execution and maintaining data consistency across distributed systems while processing real-time streaming data at scale.
learnings: Developed deep expertise in building end-to-end big data pipelines, orchestrating distributed workflows, and creating actionable insights through data visualization.

title: Large-Scale Data Processing Pipeline
description: End-to-end cloud pipeline using Medallion architecture to process 1M+ rows of European water sensor data.
fullDescription: Built an end-to-end cloud-based data pipeline using the Medallion architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold layers) in Databricks to process 1M+ rows of European water sensor data, performing scalable transformations, cleansing, and outlier detection with SQL/Scala and Spark. Automated ingestion with Azure Logic Apps and designed interactive PowerBI dashboards using DAX measures to monitor KPIs and visualize water quality trends and anomalies.
challenges: Processing and cleansing 1M+ rows of sensor data with varying quality levels while implementing effective outlier detection algorithms.
learnings: Mastered the Medallion architecture pattern for data lakes and gained proficiency in Azure cloud services and advanced Power BI dashboard development.

title: Shelf of Health: Food Processing Visualization
description: Visualization mapping grocery store shelves by food processing levels, revealing that even 'healthy' stores mainly stock ultra-processed foods.
fullDescription: Awarded Best Project Award, ranking in the top 3% of 180 students, for a creative and tangible visual design praised for its clarity and evocative storytelling. Developed an Excel-based visualization mapping grocery store shelves by food processing levels (NOVA classes), allowing users to intuitively see how 'healthy' stores still stock mostly ultra-processed foods. This project combined data analysis with creative visualization to tell a compelling story about food quality in modern grocery stores.
challenges: Creating an intuitive and engaging visualization that effectively communicates complex nutritional data to a general audience.
learnings: Learned the importance of visual storytelling in data science and how creative presentation can make data insights more accessible and impactful.

title: Culinary Trends Analysis
description: Uses machine learning and statistical testing on 84K Food.com recipes to explore how cuisine type affects ratings.
fullDescription: Used machine learning and statistical testing on 84,000 Food.com recipes to explore how cuisine type affects ratings. Built predictive models with feature engineering and SMOTE to improve accuracy and handle class imbalance. The project involved extensive data cleaning, exploratory data analysis, and the development of multiple classification models to predict recipe ratings based on various features including cuisine type, ingredients, and nutritional information.
challenges: Handling class imbalance in the dataset and extracting meaningful features from unstructured recipe data.
learnings: Gained experience in feature engineering, dealing with imbalanced datasets using SMOTE, and applying statistical methods to validate machine learning findings.
